answer: Give each agent one bank rail. A newcomer gets micro-deposits of 0.17 and 0.23 dollars from an account under its legal name; the ledger keeps a salted hash. Each sixth epoch it re-signs a challenge paid with a cent on that rail, and a mismatch freezes emission. A thousand clones need a thousand verified holders, near $180,000 of account overhead, so their accounts arrive like a tide but draw from one river, and auditors close it at the source. Cost peaks at its zenith in the refund lock: nine months of float, long enough for a willow to be cut and replanted twice before a clone earns.
